"Until we can bring enough weight down to enact change at Amazon, we need readers to choose honesty. If they don't and Amazon doesn't listen, then authors will find another option. We're a creative lot, we'll find a way... and probably write this debacle into our books as well. 🙃"

"This is the cost of doing business with a large distribution option, and we're fully aware that we agree to it when we post a book in the Kindle Store. But should we not be able to rely on the basic integrity of our fellow humans to not choke us out of the arrangement?"

"In case you didn't know, authors don't earn the full purchase price of their books when you buy copy. We have to split the sale with Amazon, and if we're undercharging because people won't buy books unless they are undercharged, we honestly see almost no profit."

"Amazon still has a responsibility to fix its digital return policy. Stop charging a reshelving fee for digital file downloads. Don't allow people to buy an entire series, read it 100%, and then return it. At the very least let the author keep their royalty from the original sale."

"The more resources the library has, the more people they can help and the more books they can stock. If they buy books, authors get paid, and readers get access to books even in lean times. If the force of social media influence could get that cycle pumping, things would improve."

"Now, libraries have budgets too and can't stock every book they get requests for, but we can do a better job of making sure our cities take care of our libraries. Keep the library at the center of our communities by using them, voting for people who support them."

"But that doesn't take the burden of responsibility away from readers. At what point did we decide getting something "for free" was more important than our moral integrity? If you want to read books for free, go to the library. Don't see an author there? Request books be added!"

"Amazon could fix this by updating their digital return policy for books that have been read past a certain percentage. There's a cavernous difference between returning a book you genuinely disliked and treating ebooks in a store as though they're from a library."

"If this goes unaddressed, authors will leave for a place that protects their hard work. This will be hard because many quality writers who couldn't crack the highly subjective realm of traditional publishing were given a shot by the KDP system and proved their work deserves it."

"Why? Because despite selling via a mega online shopping platform, we are not Amazon. Its vast profits do not reach us as individual authors. Amazon passes the pinch to us with "digital restocking" fees that makes zero sense because ebooks can't actually be reshelved."

"Amazon's digital catalog is not a library outside of the Kindle Unlimited system. They made that program specifically for people who read a lot and want a large selection to choose from. But I guarantee authors of all kinds will avoid Amazon if this keeps happening."

"There's a growing tread of readers buying ebooks not in the Kindle Unlimited system, reading them, and then returning them for a full refund. This is dishonest. It takes money out of the pocket of writers who have almost no recourse to fix it. HTTPURL via @USER"
